trajectory_rationale: A raw-material surcharge/variable pricing mechanism is described, but it is conditional and not Strong at F5.
F5 explicitly announces containerboard and box price increases; pricing was already an operating mechanism at F1, so no acceleration.
Ability to pass raw-material and energy cost increases is explicit but risk-framed rather than a Strong implemented F5 transfer.
Selling prices are commodity/market outcomes rather than a company-originated customer-economic mechanism.
Average selling-price gains are present but the frozen trajectory does not establish a Strong company-originated yield mechanism at F5.
Contracts covering the majority of volume explicitly pass aluminum/metal price changes through to customers from F1 through F5; very strong but static.
Fertilizer selling-price movements are described as market-price dynamics rather than a new company-originated customer action.
Discontinued-operation and reference-rate accounting language is non-qualifying.
Earlier selling-price increases are not carried into F5 as a qualifying Strong customer mechanism; F5 is dominated by mix and moderating raw-material costs.
Pass-through/price-increase language remains generic risk framing and is not a qualifying F5 action.
Earlier price increases offset input costs, but F5 does not retain a Strong current transfer mechanism.
F5 projects higher price realization based on current pricing, but the evidence remains below Strong and does not establish acceleration.
Discontinued-operation, financing-rate and selling-price/mix references do not establish a qualifying F5 mechanism.
